title: Termwise products of K-injective complexes on a ringed space

from.place: proof, first step, derived-functor comparison after reconstructing the truncation tower

statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian]. Let $T$ be a set, and for each $t\in T$ let $I_t^\bullet$ be a K-injective complex [def-sp-kinjective-bridge]. Assume that the product $I^n=\prod_{t\in T}I_t^n$ exists in $\mathcal A$ for every integer $n$ [def-weil-category-product]. Then the termwise product complex $I^\bullet$ is K-injective and represents the product of the objects $I_t^\bullet$ in $D(\mathcal A)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-weil-category-product].

proof.text: Mathlib isLimitConeOfHasLimitEval constructs the termwise product in complexes. Lift the legs of a cone through the full homotopy quotient and apply that limit property. Projection equations follow by functoriality. For uniqueness, lift a candidate to a chain map, convert equality of projections into homotopies and assemble their components degreewise with productHomotopy. Only limits of the evaluated family are used.

source.place: Tag 0BK6, label lemma-product-K-injective, proof of the product universal property

proof.text: Given a chain map f from an acyclic complex K to the termwise product P, each composite f ≫ P.π.app ⟨j⟩ has a homotopy to zero by Mathlib IsKInjective.homotopyZero for I j [def-sp-kinjective-bridge]. Apply the private productHomotopy assembly from Step 1 to these homotopies; zero_comp identifies the zero projection composites. This supplies the nonempty_homotopy_zero field of IsKInjective P directly. No right-orthogonality criterion or exactness of products is used.

source.place: Tag 0BK6, label lemma-product-K-injective, proof of K-injectivity

proof.text: Use the K-injective Hom comparison [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] for P and every I_t. The private mapProduct helper transfers a discrete limit through an essentially surjective functor whose maps on morphisms into the cone point and every diagram object are bijective: pull back each cone through an object preimage and the Hom bijections, lift with the original limit, and prove uniqueness using the same bijections. Apply it to Qh and the homotopy-category product of Step 1. Finally transport the limiting cone along quotientCompQhIso, obtaining exactly Q.mapCone P and thus the product [def-weil-category-product].

source.place: Tag 0BK6, label lemma-product-K-injective, final product argument

lean.statement: theorem termwise_product_isKInjective_and_isLimit {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [Abelian C] [HasDerivedCategory.{w} C] {T : Type t} (I : T → CochainComplex C ℤ) [∀ s : T, (I s).IsKInjective] [∀ n : ℤ, HasLimit (Discrete.functor I ⋙ HomologicalComplex.eval C (ComplexShape.up ℤ) n)] : let P := HomologicalComplex.coneOfHasLimitEval (Discrete.functor I) IsKInjective P.pt ∧ Nonempty (IsLimit (DerivedCategory.Q.mapCone P))
